dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: jhagitīcchāṃ samutpannām avalokya śamaṃ nayet | yata eva samudbhūtā tatas tatraiva līyate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Seeing a desire as it suddenly arises, let one bring it to rest; it dissolves back into the very place from which it arose.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: when the mind is turned inward and one sees the Self as distinct from desire, a mere play of the mind, desires dissolve like waves back into the sea. If another desire arises, shift attention from the desire to the underlying reality, the creative moment (unmeṣa) between two desires. Wallis: 'dispassionately observing a desire suddenly arising'.
dharana.technique_name: Letting a Desire Return to Its Source
dharana.instruction: Catch a desire as it arises, look at it without acting or fighting, and let it sink back.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 96 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the desire sinking back into it
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a wave rising from the sea and sinking back into the same place.
geometry.svg_hint: a single wave rising from a flat line and falling back into it
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Let it sink back
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a desire is watched as it rises and allowed to sink back where it came from, without being chased or fought. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: A desire, caught at the moment it arises
attention.secondary: Its sinking back into its source

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Seeing a desire as it suddenly arises, let one bring it to rest; it dissolves back into the very place from which it arose.
adiyogi.method_summary: When a desire arises (to check the phone, to eat, to move), catch it at the moment it appears. Look at it without acting and without fighting it. Let it settle back into where it came from, and notice the quiet there.

honesty.disclosure: Door 073 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 73 (verse 96) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 073 is dharana 73, verse 96. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This is for ordinary wants; it is not a way to ignore real needs such as hunger, rest or medical care. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit, or practise during the day. The map is a wave rising from the sea and sinking back.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: When a desire appears, catch it right away. Do not act, do not fight. Let it sink back where it came from.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a wave sinking back into the sea. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 96: seeing a desire as it suddenly arises, bring it to rest; it dissolves back into the place from which it rose.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.
